text:
- [LEXP.7.4] The `/` **operator** always produces `Float` (Python 3
  semantics), even on two `Int` values. Two integer *literals*,
  `INT_LIT / INT_LIT`, are a `Rational` literal — not an application of `/` —
  reduced at parse time ([LUNI.2.2]); any
  non-literal operand makes it the `/` operator → `Float`.

idris.name: lexp_7_2__int_op
idris.note: `/` on two Ints promotes both and yields a Float, where every other Int operator yields an Int. The parse-time Rational literal `INT_LIT / INT_LIT` is the compiler's and not modelled: the evaluator sees the operator alone.

idris.name: lexp_7_4__div_of_ints
idris.note: For every pair of Ints with a nonzero divisor, `/` is the Float quotient of their promotions. The zero divisor is [LEXP.7.15.1]'s trap, stated there; the Rational literal is not modelled.

idris.name: lexp_7_4__guarded
idris.note: `/` on two Ints once the divisor test is decided: the Float quotient, or [LEXP.7.15.1]'s trap on a zero divisor.

idris.name: lexp_7_4__quotient
idris.note: The Float quotient of two Ints: their promotions divided in IEEE arithmetic, the value `/` always produces.
